וְאַף שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "וְגַם אֶל הַנָּכְרִי אֲשֶׁר לֹא מֵעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א ח, מא

), and even though King Solomon, peace be upon him, prayed at the dedication of the Temple: "Moreover, concerning the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel... when he shall come and pray toward this house, hear in heaven" (I Kings 8:41-43),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִפְּנֵי קִידּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם: "לְמַעַן יֵדְעוּן כָּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ אֶת שְׁמֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר

", that is specifically so that Hashem, blessed be He, should answer for the sake of the sanctification of His Name, as is stated explicitly there: "in order that all the peoples of the earth may know Your Name to fear You, as do Your people Israel",
וְרַק הָאָבוֹת הֵם שֶׁחִדְּשׁוּ הַתְּפִלָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת כו:): "תְּפִלּוֹת אָבוֹת תִּקְּנוּם
", whereas intrinsic prayer was innovated solely by the Patriarchs, as our Sages taught (Berakhot 26b): "The Patriarchs instituted the daily prayers,"
וְאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִקְרְאוּ גַּם כֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת סג, א
). since Abraham (after his circumcision) and Isaac were also called by the name Israel, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Toldot, 63:1).
וְעִיקַּר תְּפִלָּה בְּיַעֲקֹב, דִּכְתִיב: "הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, כב) – קוֹלוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב נִשְׁמָע בְּבָתֵּי כְּנֵסִיּוֹת וְכוּלֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
, And the fullest perfection of prayer is realized in Jacob, as it is written: "The voice (
הַקֹּל
) is the voice (
קוֹל
) of Jacob" (Genesis 27:22)—meaning the voice of Jacob cries out in the synagogues in prayer, as expounded in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 65:20),
וְזֶה: "הַקֹּל" (חָסֵר ו') – קַל ה' (מַלְכוּת, דִּבּוּר), "קוֹל" (מָלֵא ו') – קוֹל ו' (תִּפְאֶרֶת, יַעֲקֹב, יִחוּד קוֹל וְדִבּוּר
). which is alluded to in the spelling of the two words: the first
הַקֹּל
is spelled defective without a Vav, denoting the voice of the final Hei (Malchut / Speech), while the second
קוֹל
is spelled full with a Vav, denoting the supernal Voice of Vav (Tiferet / Jacob), uniting Kol and Dibbur in prayer.

וּבְפָרָשָׁה זוֹ כְּתִיב: "וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַד שָׁם אֶת פְּנֵי ה'" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יט, כז), שֶׁמִּזֶּה נִלְמַד בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת כו:) שֶׁתִּיקֵּן אַבְרָהָם תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית, וְהַתְּפִלָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה עַל סְדוֹם

. And in this parashah it is written: "And Abraham rose early in the morning to the place where he had stood before Hashem" (Genesis 19:27), from which the Gemara (Berakhot 26b) derives that Abraham instituted the morning prayer (Shacharit), referring back to the first prayer that Abraham our father prayed on behalf of Sodom ("And Abraham remained standing before Hashem").

וְאַף שֶׁיָּדַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא יִפְעוֹל בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ להַצִּיל אֶת סְדוֹם, שֶׁלֹּא יִמָּצֵא שָׁם אַף עֲשָׂרָה צַדִּיקִים, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוֹעִילָה תְּפִלָּתוֹ לְהַצִּיל אֶת לוֹט ("וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת אַבְרָהָם וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת לוֹט מתוך ההפכה

"), Now even though Hashem, blessed be He, knew when disclosing the decree to Abraham that his prayer would not save Sodom since not even ten righteous men would be found there, nevertheless Abraham's prayer succeeded in rescuing Lot ("And God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow"),
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יָצָא דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מָצָאתִי דָּוִד עַבְדִּי" (תְּהִלִּים פט, כא), וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה נ, י): "הֵיכָן מְצָאתִיו? בִּסְדוֹם
". from whom emerged King David, peace be upon him, as it is stated: "I have found David My servant" (Psalms 89:21), on which the Midrash Rabbah (50:10) expounds: "Where did I find him? In Sodom!"
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" (תְּהִלִּים קט, ד), וְהָיָה שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר שֶׁל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
; And King David, peace be upon him, is the very root of prayer, as it is stated: "And I am prayer" (Psalms 109:4), serving as the quintessential emissary of prayer for the entirety of Israel;
וְעַל כֵּן פָּתַח הַמִּדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ מֵעִנְיַן הַתְּפִלָּה
. and for this reason Midrash Tanchuma opened this parashah with the subject of prayer.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא בְּתַנְחוּמָא (שָׁם סִימָן א): "וְהַשַּׁבָּת נִתְּנָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִקְדוּשָּׁה, לְעוֹנֶג, וְלִמְנוּחָה וְכוּלֵי
". Subsequently in that passage in Midrash Tanchuma (Vayera 1) it states: "And the Sabbath was given to Israel for holiness (kedushah), for delight (oneg), and for rest (menuchah), etc."
חָשַׁב כָּאן שָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשּׁוֹת שַׁבָּת, שֶׁהֵם קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁלֹשׁ הַסְּעוּדוֹת שֶׁנִּלְמַד בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) מִתְּלָתָא "הַיּוֹם" (שְׁמוֹת טז, כה-כו

): The Midrash enumerates here three distinct dimensions of Shabbat—holiness, delight, and rest—which correspond to the sanctity of the three Sabbath meals derived in the Gemara (Shabbat 117b end) from the three occurrences of the word "today" (ha-yom) regarding the manna (Exodus 16:25-26):
דִּכְתִיב: "אִכְלֻהוּ הַיּוֹם" – וְהַיְינוּ לְעוֹנֶג
; 1) It is written: "Eat it today (ha-yom)" – which corresponds to "for delight" (oneg); "

כִּי שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם לַה'" – הַיְינוּ לִמְנוּחָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיָּנַח בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי עַל כֵּן בֵּרַךְ ה' אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם כ, יא), וּבְמִדְרָשׁ מִשְּׁאִילְתּוֹת בְּרֵאשִׁית: "נוּחוּ בֵּיהּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנָחִי בֵּיהּ אֲנָא

"; 2) "for today (ha-yom) is a Sabbath unto Hashem" – which corresponds to "for rest" (menuchah), as it is stated: "And He rested on the seventh day; therefore Hashem blessed the Sabbath day" (Exodus 20:11), and as stated in the Midrash cited in the She'iltot (Bereishit): "Rest on it just as I rested on it"; "
הַיּוֹם לֹא תִמְצָאֻהוּ בַּשָּׂדֶה" – הַיְינוּ לִקְדוּשָּׁה, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא, ב): "וְקִדְּשׁוֹ בַּמָּן" – שֶׁלֹּא יָרַד בּוֹ כָּל עִיקָּר

. 3) "today (ha-yom) you shall not find it in the field" – which corresponds to "for holiness" (kedushah), in accordance with what they taught (Bereishit Rabbah 11:2): "'And He sanctified it' – He sanctified it through the manna," in that it did not descend on Shabbat at all.
וְנִכְתַּב בְּכָל אֶחָד לְשׁוֹן "הַיּוֹם" לְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁכָּל סְעוּדָה אוֹר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְזֶה "הַיּוֹם" מִלְּשׁוֹן "וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ה

); Now regarding each of the three meals the word "the day" (ha-yom) is written, to teach that each meal radiates a distinct spiritual illumination of its own, for "day" denotes light, as in "And God called the light Day" (Genesis 1:5);
שֶׁכָּל הַשְּׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת (מִינֵי הָאוֹר שֶׁבְּפָסוּק ג-ה), וְכָל אֶחָד אוֹר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
: for the three meals parallel the sanctity of the three Patriarchs, corresponding to the three mentions of light in the creation of the first day, each being a distinct illumination: "
יְהִי אוֹר" – זֶה אַבְרָהָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב, ה
); 1) "Let there be light (yehi ohr)" – this refers to Abraham, as they expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (2:5; 3:6); "
וַיְהִי אוֹר" – זֶה יִצְחָק, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קסז עַמּוּד א) וּבַתִּיקּוּנִים: "'יְהִי אוֹר' דָּא יְמִינָא, 'וַיְהִי אוֹר' דָּא שְׂמָאלָא

", 2) "And there was light (vayehi ohr)" – this refers to Isaac, in accordance with what is written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 167a) and in Tikkunei Zohar: "'Let there be light' is the right side (Chesed / Abraham); 'And there was light' is the left side (Gevurah / Isaac),"
וְכֵן: "'וַיְהִי אוֹר' דָּא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה דְּאִיהוּ שְׂמָאלָא", וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (תִּיקּוּן מא): "תִּשְׁרֵי וְדָא דְּרוֹעָא תִּנְיָנָא יוֹם תִּנְיָנָא", וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת יִצְחָק

; and similarly: "'And there was light' refers to Rosh Hashanah (judgment), which is the left," and as written in Tikkun 41: "Tishrei is the second arm, the second day," which is the attribute of Isaac; "
וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם" – זֶה יַעֲקֹב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם
. 3) "And God called the light Day" – this refers to Jacob, as expounded in Bereishit Rabbah there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּבְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ "יְהִי אוֹר" – הַהֶאָרָה וְהַהוֹפָעָה מֵהָאוֹר
; The inner distinction is that in Abraham our father, "Let there be light" (yehi ohr) represents the initial shining and outflow of the light (Chesed);
וְיִצְחָק – הֲוָיַת הָאוֹר, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ הֲוָיָה וּגְבוּל וְכֵלִים, וְזֶהוּ "וַיְהִי אוֹר
"; in Isaac, "And there was light" (vayehi ohr, from the root
הוה
, being) represents the bounding and substantiation of the light into enduring existence through Gevurah;
וְיַעֲקֹב הוּא הָאוֹר עַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּתוֹ ("לָאוֹר יוֹם"), שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה
. and Jacob is the perfected illumination itself ("He called the light Day"), serving as the complete chariot for the Tetragrammaton.
וְכֵן נִכְתְּבוּ הַפְּסוּקִים מֵהַסְּעוּדוֹת עַל סֵדֶר הָאָבוֹת (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יד
): And in this exact order of the three Patriarchs are written the three clauses of the verse regarding Shabbat (Isaiah 58:14): "
אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה'" – לְעוֹנֶג, נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
. 1) "Then you shall delight (tit'anag) upon Hashem" – corresponding to "for delight" (oneg), paralleling the sanctity of Abraham our father. "
וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ" – הַיְינוּ לִמְנוּחָה (נֶגֶד יִצְחָק), דִּכְתִיב: "וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ ה' לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וּמִרָּגְזֶךָ וּמִן הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה" (יְשַׁעְיָה יד, ג

), 2) "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth" – corresponding to "for rest" (menuchah, paralleling Isaac), as it is written: "And it shall come to pass in the day that Hashem shall give you rest (haniach) from your sorrow (atzbekha), and from your turmoil (rogzekha), and from the hard bondage" (Isaiah 14:3),
שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א מח רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) עַל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא יוֹם הָנִיחַ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן נְיָיחָא בַּלֵּב
: which is expounded in the holy Zohar (Part I, 48b top) regarding the Sabbath day, which is the day of rest wherein Hashem, blessed be He, grants tranquility to the heart: "
מֵעָצְבְּךָ" – מֵעֶצֶב הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁנִּקְרָא עֶצֶב, וְהַיְינוּ עַל הֶעָבָר
; "from your sorrow (atzbekha)" – from the melancholy of the evil inclination, which is called sorrow, over what has passed; "
וּמִרָּגְזֶךָ" – מֵרוֹגֶז הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְהַבָּא, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ה.): "לְעוֹלָם יַרְגִּיז אָדָם יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע

"; "and from your turmoil (rogzekha)" – from the agitation and provocation of the evil inclination regarding the future, akin to the expression (Berakhot 5a) "A person should always incite (yargiz) the good inclination against the evil inclination"; "
וּמִן הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה" – הַיְינוּ שִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת
. "and from the hard bondage" – referring to the subjugation of foreign regimes.
וְזֶהוּ "וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ" – הַיְינוּ שֶׁתִּרְכַּב וְתִשְׁלוֹט עַל חִשְׁקֵי וְתַאֲווֹת אֶרֶץ הַגְּבוֹהִים (כִּיבּוּשׁ הַיֵּצֶר, מִדַּת יִצְחָק

), And this is the meaning of "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth"—that you shall ride above and master the haughty cravings and earthly lusts (the conquest of the evil inclination, which is the Gevurah of Isaac),
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ עַל שִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח.) מִדִּכְתִיב: "וְאַתָּה עַל בָּמוֹתֵימוֹ תִדְרֹךְ" (דְּבָרִים לג, כט), וְזֶהוּ לִמְנוּחָה

. and in the Gemara (Shabbat 118a) it is likewise expounded as freedom from the subjugation of the nations, from the verse "And you shall tread upon their high places" (Deuteronomy 33:29); and all of this constitutes true rest (menuchah). "
וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ" – הַיְינוּ לִקְדוּשָּׁה, שֶׁמִּדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הוּא הַדְּבֵיקוּת בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

: 3) "And I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father" – corresponding to "for holiness" (kedushah), for the attribute of Jacob our father is cleaving (deveikut) to Hashem, blessed be He: "'
קְדֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ' – הֱיוּ קְדוֹשִׁים כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֲנִי קָדוֹשׁ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים, וְהַיְינוּ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

; as in "'You shall be holy, for I Hashem your God am holy' (Leviticus 19:2) – be holy just as I am holy," as expounded in Midrash Tanchuma, Parashat Kedoshim, which signifies the sacred union of the Holy One, blessed be He (Tiferet / Jacob), and Knesset Yisrael (Malchut);
וְזֶהוּ "נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב" – שֶׁמַּמְשִׁיךְ כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הֲוָיָ"ה לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא "שְׁלִימוּ דַּאֲבָהָתָא" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְנוּ (בְּמַאֲמָר ב
). and this is "the heritage of Jacob," who channels the entire sanctity of the Tetragrammaton into Knesset Yisrael, being the "perfection of the Patriarchs" as we explained above (in Discourse 2).
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (יִתְרוֹ פח עַמּוּד ב) נֶחְשְׁבוּ הַפְּסוּקִים בְּסֵדֶר אַחֵר
: However, in the holy Zohar (Yitro 88b), the clauses of this verse are assigned to the three Sabbath meals in a different order:

בִּסְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת כְּתִיב: "וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ", וּבִסְעוּדָתָא תִּנְיָנָא (בַּבֹּקֶר): "אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה'", וּבִסְעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית כְּתִיב: "וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ

". at the Friday night meal (corresponding to Isaac/Gevurah) it places "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth"; at the second meal on Sabbath morning (corresponding to Abraham/Chesed) it places "Then you shall delight upon Hashem"; and at the third meal (corresponding to Jacob) it places "And I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father."
וְהָעִנְיָן, שֶׁמִּצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַסֵּדֶר הוּא "אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" (מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה) וְאַחַר כָּךְ "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" (לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה

) – The explanation of this difference is that from the perspective of Hashem, blessed be He (from above to below), the order begins with "I am Hashem your God" (the root of positive commandments, Chesed) and is followed by "You shall have no other gods" (the root of negative prohibitions, Gevurah)—
שֶׁבְּדִבּוּר "אָנֹכִי" נִתְקַע תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם, וּבְדִבּוּר "לֹא יִהְיֶה" נֶעֱקַר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבָּם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א עַל פָּסוּק יִשָּׁקֵנִי

); for at the utterance of "I am," Torah study was implanted in their hearts, and at the utterance of "You shall have no," the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts, as stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (on "Let him kiss me");
וּמִצַּד הָאָדָם הַסֵּדֶר הוּא "סוּר מֵרָע" תְּחִלָּה וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב" (תְּהִלִּים לד, טו

). whereas from the perspective of human service (working from below to above), the necessary order is first "Turn away from evil" (subduing the evil inclination, Gevurah) and only afterward "and do good" (Psalms 34:15).

וְכֵן כָּאן, מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַסֵּדֶר הוּא לִזְכּוֹת תְּחִלָּה בְּלֵיל שַׁבָּת לְ"וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ" – שֶׁהוּא הַנְּיָיחָא מֵעֶצֶב וְרוֹגֶז הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁהוּא שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה, וּמִמֵּילָא נִיצּוֹל מִשִּׁעְבּוּד

; So too here: from the side of Israel's upward progression through the Sabbath meals (in the Zohar), the order begins on Friday night with meriting "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth"—which is resting and breaking free from the sorrow and agitation of the evil inclination (the leaven in the dough) and from foreign subjugation ("turn away from evil");

וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת: "אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה'" – שֶׁהוּא לִזְכּוֹת לִבְחִינַת עֹנֶ"ג (רָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת: עֵדֶן, נָהָר, גַּן), "לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחְמִי" (מִשְׁלֵי ט, ה), לִזְכּוֹת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, עוֹנֶג מֵעֵדֶן עִלָּאָה, וְזֶהוּ "בֵּרְכוֹ בַּמָּן" שֶׁהוּא לֶחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
. and afterward on Sabbath morning one ascends to "Then you shall delight upon Hashem"—attaining the level of
עֹנֶג

(an acronym for Eden, Nahar River, Gan Garden), "Come, eat of My bread" (Proverbs 9:5), meriting the delight of Torah from the supernal Eden ("and do good"), which corresponds to "He blessed it with the manna," the bread from heaven.

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּישַׁעְיָה, שֶׁנִּסְדַּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁבָּא הַשָּׂכָר מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "אָז תִּתְעַנַּג" תְּחִלָּה וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ", כְּסֵדֶר "אָנֹכִי" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "לֹא יִהְיֶה

". In contrast, in the verse in Isaiah, which is ordered according to how the reward flows down from Hashem, blessed be He, "Then you shall delight" comes first and is followed by "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth," matching the divine order of "I am" followed by "You shall have no."
וְכֵן כְּשֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נַפְשׁוֹת הָאָבוֹת, נוֹלַד מִתְּחִלָּה אַבְרָהָם וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִצְחָק
; Similarly, when Hashem, blessed be He, brought the souls of the Patriarchs into the world, Abraham (Chesed) was born first and afterward Isaac (Gevurah);
וּבִסְעוּדוֹת שַׁבָּת שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנֶּחְשָׁב כְּנֶגְדָּן, נֶחְשָׁב מִקּוֹדֶם סְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת נֶגֶד יִצְחָק וְאַחַר כָּךְ סְעוּדַת יוֹם שַׁבָּת כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם

, whereas in the Sabbath meals of Israel which parallel them (and just as in the cycle of the day, night precedes day), the Friday night meal corresponding to Isaac comes first, followed by the Sabbath daytime meal corresponding to Abraham,
כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא הַסֵּדֶר מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל לִזְכּוֹת וּלְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לִזְכּוֹת לִקְדוּשַּׁת הָאָבוֹת
. in accordance with the upward order through which Israel must strive to attain the sanctity of the Patriarchs.
וּבְפָרָשַׁת "וַיְכֻלּוּ" בָּא הַסֵּדֶר: "וַיִּשְׁבֹּת בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי" – שֶׁהוּא הַמְּנוּחָה
; Now in the Torah's account of Shabbat in Vayekhullu (Genesis 2:2-3), the order is: first "And He rested (vayishbot) on the seventh day"—which is rest (menuchah);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי" – שֶׁהוּא "בֵּרְכוֹ בַּמָּן" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יא, ב), וְהַיְינוּ עוֹנֶג שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עֵדֶן נָהָר גַּן
and second, "And God blessed (vayevarekh) the seventh day"—which is "He blessed it with the manna" as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (11:2), representing delight (oneg: Eden, Nahar, Gan) (
וְכֵן כְּתִיב: "בִּרְכַּת ה' הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר" [מִשְׁלֵי י, כב], וְנִדְרַשׁ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם: זוֹ הַשַּׁבָּת
, (and similarly it is written: "The blessing of Hashem, it makes rich" Proverbs 10:22, which is expounded in Bereishit Rabbah there as referring to Shabbat,

וְהָעוֹשֶׁר בָּא עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָה וְעוֹנֶג לִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שָׁם מֵהַטַּבָּח, וְשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְעוֹשֶׁר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁמְּכַבְּדִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם וּבַגְּמָרָא שַׁבָּת קיט

.); for wealth comes through eating and delighting to honor the Shabbat, as illustrated in the Midrash Rabbah there by the story of Joseph who honored Shabbat and inherited the pearls of the hatmaker/butcher, and as taught in the Gemara, Shabbat 119a, that the wealthy merit riches because they honor Shabbat);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ" – לִקְדוּשָּׁה
. and third, "and He sanctified it (vayekaddesh oto)"—corresponding to holiness (kedushah).

וְהַטַּעַם (שֶׁהִקְדִּים "וַיִּשְׁבֹּת" לְ"וַיְבָרֶךְ"), דְּשָׁם מְדַבֵּר בְּ"וַיִּשְׁבֹּת" שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה לוֹ נְיָיחָא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ וּמָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָיו כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה

, The reason why Vayekhullu places "And He rested" (menuchah) before "And He blessed" (oneg) is that there "And He rested" speaks primarily of Hashem, blessed be He, experiencing satisfaction and rest in His completed world, which found favor in His eyes, as stated in Midrash Rabbah;
רַק מִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה גַּם הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל לִנְיָיחָא – "נוּחוּ בֵּיהּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנָחִי בֵּיהּ אֲנָא
". and as a natural consequence of His resting, Israel likewise merits rest: "Rest on it just as I rested on it."
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן "וַיְבָרֶךְ" וְ"וַיְקַדֵּשׁ" שֶׁהוּא נִיתָּן יְשִׁירוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
: In contrast, "And He blessed" and "and He sanctified" speak of what He directly bestowed upon Israel (and between those two, blessing/oneg precedes sanctification/kedushah):
הַבְּרָכָה – "אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה
'"; the blessing is "Then you shall delight upon Hashem"; "

וַיְקַדֵּשׁ" – הוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת י:): "מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמָהּ, וַאֲנִי מְבַקֵּשׁ לִתְּנָהּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל", וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לָדַעַת כִּי אֲנִי ה' מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם" (שְׁמוֹת לא, יג

), and "He sanctified it" refers to what they taught (Shabbat 10b): "I have a precious gift in My treasury, and Shabbat is its name, and I seek to give it to Israel; go and inform them, as it is stated: 'to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you'" (Exodus 31:13)—
וְלֹא נִזְכַּר כָּאן בַּנְּתִינָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל רַק שְׁתֵּי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת: עוֹנֶג ("וַיְבָרֶךְ") וּקְדוּשָּׁה ("וַיְקַדֵּשׁ
"). so that regarding the direct bestowal to Israel in Vayekhullu, only the two levels of delight (blessing) and holiness (sanctification) are mentioned, ordered from Chesed to Tiferet.

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יְשַׁעְיָה שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר מֵהַשָּׂכָר שֶׁנּוֹתֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁבִיל הַשַּׁבָּת, בָּא הַסֵּדֶר כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "אָז תִּתְעַנַּג" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ", כְּסֵדֶר הַדִּבְּרוֹת "אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה

"; Whereas in Isaiah, which speaks of all three as rewards bestowed by Hashem, blessed be He, upon Israel for observing Shabbat, the order follows the downward flow from Hashem: "Then you shall delight" (Chesed) followed by "And I will make you ride" (Gevurah), like "I am" and "You shall have no";
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ נִסְדַּר כְּסֵדֶר הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל: "סוּר מֵרָע" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב" – "וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "אָז תִּתְעַנַּג" כָּאָמוּר

. while in the holy Zohar (and in the Tanchuma: "for holiness entering Shabbat, for delight, and for rest"), it is arranged according to the order of human effort by Israel: "turn away from evil" ("And I will make you ride") and afterward "do good" ("Then you shall delight"), as explained.

וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְסַיֵּים בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא שָׁם: "אֵלּוּ שֶׁבַע בְּרָכוֹת שֶׁמִּתְפַּלְּלִין בְּשַׁבָּת. וְאֵיזֶה זֶה יוֹם הַמְּיוּחָד וְהַמְּנוּחָה שֶׁאֵין כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ? זֶה הַשַּׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי

", And afterward the Midrash Tanchuma concludes there: "These correspond to the seven blessings that we pray on Shabbat. And which is this unique day and rest unlike any other? This is the Shabbat, etc."
וְלֹא זָכַר כָּאן מִשְּׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשּׁוֹת שַׁבָּת רַק הַמְּנוּחָה
. Here at the conclusion, out of the three dimensions of Shabbat, the Midrash mentions only "rest" (menuchah).
וְהַטַּעַם, שֶׁבְּפָרָשַׁת "וַיְכֻלּוּ" נִזְכַּר רַק "בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי", וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִקְרָא הַיּוֹם בַּתּוֹרָה בְּשֵׁם "שַׁבָּת" (עַל שֵׁם "וַיִּשְׁבֹּת
"), The reason is that in Vayekhullu the day is initially called only "the seventh day," and subsequently throughout the Torah it is named "Shabbat" (after vayishbot, "and He rested"),
שֶׁהָעִיקָּר מַה שֶּׁנִּיתַּן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא הַשְּׁבִיתָה בְּשַׁבָּת
; because the foundational mitzvah commanded to Israel in the Written Torah is the cessation of labor (shevitah) on Shabbat;
שֶׁמִּצְוַת עוֹנֶג לֹא בָּא בַּתּוֹרָה בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַק בְּרֶמֶז בִּתְלָתָא "הַיּוֹם", וְעִיקָּרוֹ מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי קַבָּלָה ("וְקָרָאתָ לַשַּׁבָּת עֹנֶג

"), whereas the mitzvah of delighting (oneg) on Shabbat is not stated explicitly in the Pentateuch, appearing only by way of allusion in the three occurrences of "today" (ha-yom) and articulated explicitly in the Prophets ("And you shall call the Shabbat a delight" Isaiah 58:13);
וְנִקְרָא הַיּוֹם רַק עַל שֵׁם הַמְּנוּחָה – "שַׁבָּת", שֶׁהוּא "נוּחוּ בֵּיהּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנָחִי בֵּיהּ אֲנָא
". and therefore the day itself is named strictly after rest—"Shabbat"—which is "Rest on it just as I rested on it."
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מח, ד): רַבִּי יִצְחָק פָּתַח: "מִזְבַּח אֲדָמָה תַּעֲשֶׂה לִּי וְגוֹמֵר בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ" (שְׁמוֹת כ, כא

) – In Midrash Rabbah (Parashah 48:4): Rabbi Yitzchak opened his discourse: "'An altar of earth you shall make unto Me... in every place where I cause My name to be mentioned I will come unto you and bless you' (Exodus 20:21) –
מָה אִם זֶה שֶׁבָּנָה מִזְבֵּחַ לִשְׁמִי הֲרֵינִי נִגְלֶה עָלָיו וּמְבָרְכוֹ, אַבְרָהָם שֶׁמָּל עַצְמוֹ לִשְׁמִי עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה (שֶׁאֶתְגַּלֶּה עָלָיו, דִּכְתִיב: וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו ה
'). if regarding one who merely builds an altar of earth for My Name, behold, I am revealed to him and bless him, then regarding Abraham who circumcised his own flesh for My Name, how much more so!"
יֵשׁ לְהָבִין, הֵיכָן נִזְכַּר כָּאן שֶׁבֵּרַךְ לְאַבְרָהָם
? We must understand: where is there any mention here at the beginning of Vayera that God blessed Abraham?
בִּשְׁלָמָא שָׁם בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ כְּתִיב: "אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ", מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּאַבְרָהָם לֹא נִזְכַּר כָּאן רַק שֶׁנִּגְלָה עָלָיו ("וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו ה'") וְלֹא הוּזְכַּר בְּרָכָה

! Granted, there regarding the altar it is explicitly written, "I will come unto you and bless you"; whereas here regarding Abraham it states only that He appeared to him ("And Hashem appeared to him"), without mentioning any blessing!

גַּם מַה שֶּׁאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מח, ה): "וְשׁוֹר וָאַיִל לִשְׁלָמִים לִזְבֹּחַ לִפְנֵי ה'... מָה אִם זֶה שֶׁהִקְרִיב שׁוֹר וָאַיִל לִשְׁמִי הֲרֵינִי נִגְלֶה עָלָיו וּמְבָרְכוֹ וְכוּלֵי

", Furthermore, regarding what Rabbi Levi says immediately afterward in Midrash Rabbah (48:5) on the verse "And an ox and a ram for peace-offerings, to sacrifice before Hashem... for today Hashem appears to you" (Leviticus 9:4): "If regarding one who offered an ox and a ram for My Name, behold, I am revealed to him and bless him, Abraham who circumcised himself for My Name, how much more so!"—
יֵשׁ לְהָבִין, דְּהָא גַּם שָׁם לֹא הוּזְכַּר בְּרָכָה, וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב אַחַר כָּךְ "וַיֵּצְאוּ וַיְבָרֲכוּ אֶת הָעָם" (וַיִּקְרָא ט, כג) רָחוֹק מִפָּסוּק "וְשׁוֹר וָאַיִל

"! this too requires explanation, for in that verse (Leviticus 9:4) no blessing is mentioned either, and what is written much later at the end of the chapter, "And Moses and Aaron went out and blessed the people" (Leviticus 9:23), is far removed from the verse "And an ox and a ram"!
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן, דְּעִיקַּר בְּרָכָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
, However, the explanation is that the essential blessing of Hashem, blessed be He, consists of the illumination and expansion of words of Torah,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ סֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר (סִימָן ג): "וּמְנָלַן דְּאִיקְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּרָכָה? דִּכְתִיב: וּמָלֵא בִּרְכַּת ה' יָם וְדָרוֹם יְרָשָׁה (דְּבָרִים לג, כג), וּכְתִיב בַּתּוֹרָה: וּרְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם (אִיּוֹב יא, ט)", עַיֵּין שָׁם

. just as is written at the beginning of Sefer HaBahir (section 3): "And from where do we know that the Torah is called 'blessing' (berakhah)? Because it is written: 'And full of the blessing of Hashem, possess the sea (yam) and the south' (Deuteronomy 33:23), and regarding the Torah it is written: 'And broader than the sea (yam)' (Job 11:9)," see there.
וְהַיְינוּ רִיבּוּי בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר "וּרְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם", דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב אוֹתִיּוֹתֶיהָ סְפוּרוֹת וּמְנוּיוֹת

. And this refers specifically to the boundless expansion of the Oral Torah (berakhah from the root bereikhah, a flowing spring), concerning which it is said "and broader than the sea," since the letters of the Written Torah are fixed and counted.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ" – בִּרְכַּת ה' הוּא רִיבּוּי בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה

. Thus, the inner meaning of "In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned I will come unto you and bless you" is that the revelation of Hashem's presence ("I will come unto you") brings the blessing of Hashem—the wellspring of the Oral Torah.
וְכֵן כָּאן דִּכְתִיב: "וַיֵּרָא אֵלָי"ו ה'", שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז שֶׁהוֹפִיעַ מִי' חָכְמָה עַל יְדֵי ו' הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת וְהוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
, And so it is right here in the words "And Hashem appeared
אֵלָיו
(to him)": as we explained above (in Discourse 3), the word
אֵלָיו (אֶל י' ו
') signifies that the supernal light shone from Yud (Chokhmah) through Vav (the middle bar, Tiferet) into the attribute of Malchut, which is the Oral Torah,
וְכֵן כָּל הָאָמוּר בַּפָּרָשָׁה מְרַמֵּז שֶׁזָּכָה לְאוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
, and indeed everything recounted in this parashah alludes to Abraham meriting the light of the Oral Torah,
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: "עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה שֶׁהֲרֵינִי נִגְלֶה עָלָיו וּמְבָרְכוֹ" – בְּאוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה (הַכָּלוּל בְּתֵיבַת "וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו
"). which is why Rabbi Yitzchak said: "how much more so that I am revealed to him and bless him"—for the very phrase "And He appeared
אֵלָיו
" embodies the blessing of the light of the Oral Torah.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַיְיתֵי מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְשׁוֹר וָאַיִל לִשְׁלָמִים לִזְבֹּחַ לִפְנֵי ה'" (וַיִּקְרָא ט, ד), וְהַיְינוּ לַמִּדָּה שֶׁ"לִּפְנֵי" שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה (כֶּתֶר, עַתִּיקָא

), And afterward Rabbi Levi brings a second derivation from what is stated: "And an ox and a ram for peace-offerings, to sacrifice before (lifnei) Hashem" (Leviticus 9:4)—where "before Hashem" alludes to the supernal level that precedes the four letters of the Tetragrammaton,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפָרֵשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג עט עַמּוּד ב) הַלָּשׁוֹן "עַל ה'" שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְמַזָּלָא קַדִּישָׁא שֶׁהוּא עַתִּיקָא
, just as the holy Zohar (Part III, 79b) explains the phrase "above Hashem (al Hashem)" as referring to Mazala Kadisha (the Holy Constellation), which is Atika (Keter),
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם סה עַמּוּד ב) דְּקוֹצָא דְּיוּ"ד דִּלְעֵילָא רְמִיזָא לְאַיִן, כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן, וְהַיְינוּ "עַל ה'" – עַל אוֹתִיּוֹת הֲוָיָ"ה
; based on what is written (there, 65b) that the upper thorn of the Yud alludes to Ayin (Nothingness), Keter Elyon, which stands "above Hashem"—above the four letters of the Tetragrammaton;
וְכֵן מוֹרֶה "לִפְנֵי ה'" עַל מִדַּת עַתִּיקָא שֶׁלִּפְנֵי ה
'. and similarly the phrase "before Hashem (lifnei Hashem)" signifies the level of Atika which precedes the Tetragrammaton.
וְזֶה זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי "שׁוֹר וָאַיִל" לְאוֹר טַלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא שֶׁמּוֹפִיעַ בְּלֵב הַחֲכָמִים אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהוּא אוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּגְנַז לַעֲמֵלֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה

. And through the peace-offerings of the "ox and ram" offered "before Hashem," they merited drawing down the supernal dew of Atika (tala de-Atika) which illuminates within the hearts of the sages the light of the Oral Torah—the primordial light of Creation that was hidden away for those who toil in the Oral Torah.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: "הֲרֵינִי נִגְלֶה עָלָיו וּמְבָרְכוֹ" – רִיבּוּי בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְלָמַד קַל וָחוֹמֶר לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְאוֹר זֶה עַל יְדֵי הַמִּילָה

. And this is what Rabbi Levi meant by "behold, I am revealed to him and bless him"—bestowing the supernal blessing and abundance of the Oral Torah from Atika—and from this he derived by kal va-chomer that Abraham our father merited this very illumination through the covenant of circumcision.
קוֹדֶם סְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת אוֹמְרִים "אֵשֶׁת חַיִל מִי יִמְצָא וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי לא, י
), Prior to the Friday night meal we recite the hymn "A woman of valor (Eshet Chayil), who can find? etc." (Proverbs 31:10),
דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא "אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה'" (שָׁם לא, ל
). because Knesset Yisrael (the Ecclesia of Israel / the Shechinah) is the archetypal "woman who fears Hashem" (Proverbs 31:30).
וְזֶה בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַשִּׂיג הַיִּרְאָה, דְּשׁוֹמְרֵי שַׁבָּת נִקְרְאוּ "יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי" (בְּתַעֲנִית ח
:). And this is realized on Shabbat, when every individual in Israel attains awe of Heaven, for those who observe Shabbat are called "those who fear My Name" (Ta'anit 8b).
וּבִכְנִיסַת שַׁבָּת כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכֶה לִנְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה, נִשְׁמָתִין חַדְתִּין
, Upon the entry of Shabbat, every single Jew merits an additional soul (neshamah yeteirah)—renewed supernal souls—
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח עַמּוּד ב): "נִשְׁמְתָא דְּכָל שְׁלִימוּ בַּהּ כְּדוּגְמָא דְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי, וּבְגִין כָּךְ אִיקְרֵי שַׁבָּת", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. as is written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 88b): "a soul in which all perfection resides, after the pattern of the World to Come, and on account of this it is called Shabbat," see there.
וְשַׁבָּת נִקְרְאָה כַּלָּה מַלְכְּתָא, וְנִקְרְאוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל "אֵשֶׁת חַיִל עֲטֶרֶת בַּעְלָהּ" (מִשְׁלֵי יב, ד
). Thus Shabbat is called the Bride and Queen (Kallah Malketa), and all of Israel are called "a woman of valor, who is the crown of her husband" (Proverbs 12:4).

וּבְמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חַיֵּי שָׂרָה ד) נִדְרַשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ דְּ"אֵשֶׁת חַיִל" עַל שָׂרָה, שֶׁהָיְתָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה יָצְאָה כָּל אוּמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית – כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

, In Midrash Tanchuma on this parashah (Chayei Sarah 4), this entire chapter of "Eshet Chayil" is expounded regarding Sarah our mother, who was the very first matriarch from whom emerged the entire Israelite nation—Knesset Yisrael—
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הַבִּיטוּ אֶל אַבְרָהָם אֲבִיכֶם וְאֶל שָׂרָה תְּחוֹלֶלְכֶם" (יְשַׁעְיָה נא, ב
); as it is stated: "Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah who bore you" (Isaiah 51:2);
דְּאַבְרָהָם הָיָה אָב רִאשׁוֹן וְשָׂרָה אֵם רִאשׁוֹנָה
, for Abraham was the first father and Sarah the first mother,
וְאִיתָא (בְּרָכוֹת לה:): "אֵין אָבִיו אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְאֵין אִמּוֹ אֶלָּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
", paralleling what is stated in the Gemara (Berakhot 35b): "'Your father' refers to none other than the Holy One, blessed be He, and 'your mother' refers to none other than Knesset Yisrael,"
וּמָצִינוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין לא:) בְּרַב יוֹסֵף: "כִּי הֲוָה שָׁמַע קָל כַּרְעֵי דְּאִמֵּיהּ, אָמַר: אֵיקוּם מִקַּמֵּי שְׁכִינְתָּא דְּאָתְיָא
". and thus we find (Kiddushin 31b) regarding Rav Yosef: "When he heard the sound of his mother's footsteps approaching, he would say: 'Let me arise before the approaching Shechinah!'"
וְעַל כֵּן שָׂרָה שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵם רִאשׁוֹנָה לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִדְרַשׁ עָלֶיהָ כָּל "אֵשֶׁת חַיִל
". Therefore, because Sarah was the primal mother of all Israel and the earthly chariot for Knesset Yisrael, the entire hymn of "Eshet Chayil" is expounded upon her.
וְדָרַשׁ שָׁם: "'זָמְמָה שָׂדֶה וַתִּקָּחֵהוּ' (מִשְׁלֵי לא, טז) – זָמְמָה וְנָטְלָה שְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה וְכוּלֵי
". Now the Midrash Tanchuma there expounds: "'She considers a field and buys it' (Proverbs 31:16) – she considered and took the field of Machpelah, etc."

וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין: הָא בְּחַיֶּיהָ לֹא יָדְעָה שָׂרָה מִשְּׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה, רַק אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ קָנָה הַשָּׂדֶה אַחַר מוֹתָהּ וּקְבָרָהּ שָׁם, וְאֵיךְ נִדְרַשׁ עָלֶיהָ "זָמְמָה שָׂדֶה וַתִּקָּחֵהוּ

"? This requires explanation: during her lifetime Sarah knew nothing of the purchase of the field of Machpelah; rather, Abraham our father bought the field after her passing and buried her there—so how can it be expounded of Sarah that "she considered a field and acquired it"?
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חַיֵּי שָׂרָה קכט עַמּוּד א
): However, the matter is understood based on what is written in the holy Zohar (Chayei Sarah 129a): "

רָזָא דְּמִלָּה: 'שְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה' וַדַּאי. מַאן מַכְפֵּלָה? הֵ"א דְּבִשְׁמָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּאִיהִי מַכְפֵּלָה וְכוּלֵי, דְּלָא הֲוֵי בִּשְׁמָא קַדִּישָׁא אָת אַחֲרָא מַכְפֵּלָה בַּר אִיהִי", עַיֵּין שָׁם

. "The mystery of the matter is that it is written 'the field of ha-Machpelah' (the double one, modifying the feminine 'ha-me'arah' rather than 'sadeh kaful'). Who is 'the double one' (ha-Machpelah)? It is the letter Hei of the Holy Name (
יהוה
), which is doubled... for there is no other letter in the Holy Name that is doubled except for Her," see there.
וְהַיְינוּ הֵ"א עִלָּאָה וְהֵ"א תַּתָּאָה, שֶׁהוּא שְׁכִינְתָּא עִלָּאָה וּשְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה
. That is to say, it refers to the upper Hei (Binah) and the lower Hei (Malchut) of the Tetragrammaton, which are the Upper Shechinah and the Lower Shechinah.
וּלְעֵיל מִינַּהּ אָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "כְּגַוְונָא דָּא כְּתִיב: 'כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה'' (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, כז) – לְעֵילָא וְתַתָּא וְכוּלֵי

", Just prior to this, the holy Zohar stated: "In the same manner it is written: 'See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field which Hashem has blessed' (Genesis 27:27) – above and below, etc.,"
וְהַיְינוּ דִּשְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה, כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, נִקְרְאָה "שָׂדֶה
", meaning that the Lower Shechinah, Knesset Yisrael, is called a "field" (sadeh),
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה'" – שֶׁמִּדָּה זוֹ הִיא שַׁבָּת, וּכְתִיב בּוֹ מְפוֹרָשׁ: "וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ג
); which is why it is described as "a field which Hashem has blessed"—for this attribute is Shabbat, concerning which it is explicitly written: "And God blessed the seventh day" (Genesis 2:3);
וּמִדָּה זוֹ נִקְרְאָה "שָׂדֶה" עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (כְּתוּבּוֹת ב: דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל נִסְתַּחְפָּה) שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה נִקְרֵאת שָׂדֶה שֶׁל הַבַּעַל, עַיֵּין שָׁם
. and this feminine attribute (Malchut) is termed a "field" in the same way that Tosafot write (Ketubot 2b, s.v. Nistachfah) that a wife is called the field of her husband, see there.

וְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה סה) שֶׁבְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנִּכְנַס יַעֲקֹב אֵצֶל אָבִיו נִכְנְסָה עִמּוֹ גַּן עֵדֶן, הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב: "רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה'", וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד

: And it is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, end of Parashah 65) that when Jacob entered before his father Isaac, the fragrance of the Garden of Eden (Gan Eden) entered with him, as it is written: "See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field which Hashem has blessed"—and all of these concepts are one:
דְּגַן עֵדֶן הוּא מִשְׁכַּן נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְ"גַן" הוּא שְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א כו עַמּוּד א
). for Gan Eden is the abode of the souls of Israel, and "the Garden" (Gan) is the Lower Shechinah (Malchut), as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 26a).
וְיֵשׁ גַּן עֵדֶן שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה וְגַן עֵדֶן שֶׁלְּמַטָּה, וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קפב עַמּוּד ב
): Now there is the Upper Gan Eden and the Lower Gan Eden, which corresponds to what is written in the holy Zohar (Part III, 182b): "
הַאי עֵדֶן תַּתָּאָה אִיקְרֵי גַּן לְעֵדֶן דִּלְעֵילָא, וְהַאי גַּן אִיקְרֵי עֵדֶן לְגַן דִּלְתַתָּא

"; "This lower Eden (Binah) is called a 'Garden' (Gan) in relation to the supernal Eden (Keter / Chokhmah), while this very 'Garden' (Binah) is called 'Eden' in relation to the lower Garden (Malchut)";

וְהַיְינוּ דְּהֵ"א עִלָּאָה (בִּינָה) אִיקְרֵי "גַּן" לְעֵדֶן דִּלְעֵילָא שֶׁהוּא כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (תִּיקּוּן נה וּבַהַקְדָּמָה) שֶׁהוּא מִקּוֹצָא דְּיוּ"ד דִּלְעֵילָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ

, meaning that the upper Hei (Binah) is called a "Garden" relative to the supernal Eden, which is Keter Elyon—as written in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 55 and in the Introduction), emanating from the upper thorn of the Yud—

וְהַאי גַּן (בִּינָה) אִיקְרֵי "עֵדֶן" לְגַן דִּלְתַתָּא (מַלְכוּת), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א שָׁם): "'וְנָהָר יֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן' – דָּא אִמָּא עִלָּאָה (בִּינָה), 'לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן' – דָּא שְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה (מַלְכוּת

)". and this same upper Garden (Binah) is called "Eden" relative to the lower Garden (Malchut), just as is written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 26a) on Genesis 2:10: "'And a river went out of Eden' – this is the Upper Mother (Binah), 'to water the garden' – this is the Lower Shechinah (Malchut)."
וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "'כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה'' – לְעֵילָא וְתַתָּא
". And this is what the holy Zohar meant by "'like the smell of a field which Hashem has blessed' – above and below."

וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (שָׁם סה, כב): "'וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו' – כְּגוֹן יוֹסֵף מְשִׁיתָא וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם, וְדָרַשׁ "בְּגָדָיו" כְּמוֹ "בּוֹגְדָיו", וְכֵן הוּא בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין לז

.), This also illuminates what is written in Midrash Rabbah (65:22) on the beginning of that verse, "'And he smelled the smell of his garments (begadav)' – such as Yosef Meshita and Yakim of Tzerorot (sinners who repented in a single moment of martyrdom)," where they expounded begadav ("his garments") as bogedav ("his betrayers"), as also cited in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 37a):

וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה'" – וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשָּׂדֶה (הֵ"א תַּתָּאָה) מִתְבָּרֵךְ מֵהֵ"א עִלָּאָה שֶׁהוּא בִּינָה, תְּשׁוּבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, י

). for concerning their penitence Isaac proclaimed, "See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field (the lower Hei) which Hashem has blessed" – blessed by the upper Hei, which is Binah, the source of repentance (teshuvah), as it is stated: "And his heart will understand (yavin) and he will repent (vashav)" (Isaiah 6:10).
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר: "וּבְגִין כָּךְ 'שְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה' וַדַּאי, וְלֹא שָׂדֶה כָּפוּל", וְהַיְינוּ הֵ"א עִלָּאָה וְהֵ"א תַּתָּאָה

. And this is why the Zohar emphasized: "Therefore it is certainly written 'the field of ha-Machpelah' (the doubled Hei), and not 'a double field' (sadeh kaful)"—signifying the union of the upper Hei and the lower Hei.

וּמִקּוֹדֶם אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם קכח עַמּוּד ב): "כְּגַוְונָא דָּא יְרוּשָׁלַיִם לְעֵילָא וִירוּשָׁלַיִם לְתַתָּא, אֲחִידָא לְעֵילָא וַאֲחִידָא לְתַתָּא וְכוּלֵי, בְּגִין כָּךְ כְּפֵלְתָּא הִיא וְכוּלֵי

", Earlier in that passage in the holy Zohar (128b) it states: "In the same manner there is Jerusalem above (Binah) and Jerusalem below (Malchut); it is bound above and bound below, and therefore it is doubled (Machpelah), etc.,"

וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת פְּקוּדֵי) שֶׁיְּרוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁל מַעְלָה מְכֻוֶּונֶת כְּנֶגֶד יְרוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁל מַטָּה וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "יְרוּשָׁלַיִם הַבְּנוּיָה כְּעִיר שֶׁחֻבְּרָה לָּהּ יַחְדָּו" (תְּהִלִּים קכב, ג), עַיֵּין שָׁם, וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא (תַּעֲנִית ה

.). which aligns with what is written in Midrash Tanchuma (beginning of Parashat Pekudei), that Jerusalem above is aligned directly opposite Jerusalem below, as it is stated: "Jerusalem, built as a city that is joined together" (Psalms 122:3), see there, and as similarly expounded in the Gemara (Ta'anit 5a).
וּלְעֵיל בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חַיֵּי שָׂרָה קכב עַמּוּד א) דָּרַשׁ הַפָּסוּק "מֶלֶךְ לְשָׂדֶה נֶעֱבָד" (קֹהֶלֶת ה, ח
): And at the beginning of the parashah in the holy Zohar (122a), it expounds the verse "A king is bound to the cultivated field" (Ecclesiastes 5:8): "
מַאן מֶלֶךְ? דָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא; 'לְשָׂדֶה נֶעֱבָד' – כַּד אִתְתַּקַּן כִּדְקָא יָאוֹת וְכוּלֵי, דָּא שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה' וְכוּלֵי
, "Who is 'a king'? This is the Holy One, blessed be He; 'to a cultivated field' – when the field is rectified and cultivated as is fitting, etc., this is 'the field which Hashem has blessed,' etc.,
דְּכַד אִיהוּ נֶעֱבָד וְאִתְתַּקַּן וְכוּלֵי כִּדְקָא יָאוֹת, כְּדֵין מֶלֶךְ עִלָּאָה אִתְחַבַּר עִמַּהּ", עַיֵּין שָׁם; דָּרַשׁ "נֶעֱבָד" עַל הַשָּׂדֶה שֶׁהִיא נֶעֱבָד כָּרָאוּי
. for when this field is cultivated and rectified properly through mitzvot, then the Supernal King unites with Her," see there—reading ne'evad as modifying the field when properly cultivated.

וְשָׂרָה שֶׁהוֹלִידָה אֶת יִצְחָק שֶׁהָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה יָמִים – הַתְחָלַת צְמִיחַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל – דָּרַשׁ עָלֶיהָ: "זָמְמָה שָׂדֶה וַתִּקָּחֵהוּ", שֶׁזָּכְתָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ לִהְיוֹת מֶרְכָּבָה לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל (שְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה

). Thus, regarding Sarah, who gave birth to Isaac—the first child circumcised on the eighth day, marking the initial sprouting of Knesset Yisrael—the Midrash expounds: "She considered a field and acquired it," meaning that during her lifetime she merited to acquire and embody the spiritual reality of Knesset Yisrael, the "field of ha-Machpelah" (which is why she was subsequently buried there).
וְכֵן דָּרַשׁ בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא אַחַר כָּךְ עַל סֵיפָא דִּקְרָא: "'מִפְּרִי כַפֶּיהָ נָטְעָה כָּרֶם' – זֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי כֶרֶם ה' צְבָאוֹת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל (יְשַׁעְיָה ה, ז

)". And this explains what the Midrash Tanchuma expounds immediately afterward on the second half of that very verse: "'From the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard' (Proverbs 31:16) – this refers to Israel, as it is stated: 'For the vineyard of Hashem of Hosts is the house of Israel'" (Isaiah 5:7).
וְלִכְאוֹרָה אֵיזוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת יֵשׁ לָזֶה לְרֹאשׁ הַפָּסוּק "זָמְמָה שָׂדֶה וַתִּקָּחֵהוּ" שֶׁדָּרַשׁ עַל שְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה

? For on the surface, what connection does planting the nation of Israel in the second half of the verse have to the first half of the verse, "She considers a field and buys it," which the Midrash explained as the field of Machpelah?
אַךְ לְפִי הָאָמוּר מְבוֹאָר הֵיטֵב: "זָמְמָה שָׂדֶה" – הֵ"א דְּבִשְׁמָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּאִיהִי מַכְפֵּלָה, שְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה; "וַתִּקָּחֵהוּ" – שֶׁזָּכְתָה לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

; However, according to what we have explained, the two halves of the verse flow together seamlessly: "She considers a field" – the doubled letter Hei of the Holy Name, which is the spiritual "field of ha-Machpelah"; "and she acquires it" – she merited to become the embodiment of Knesset Yisrael;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "'מִפְּרִי כַפֶּיהָ נָטְעָה כָּרֶם' – זֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל", שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה יָצְאָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, אוּמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית, וְהִיא אֵם הָאוּמָּה כָּאָמוּר

. and consequently, "'from the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard' – this is Israel," for out of her acquisition of that spiritual field emerged the vineyard of the Israelite nation, she being the Mother of the nation as stated.
רַק הַתַּנְחוּמָא הִפְסִיק בְּדְרָשַׁת הַפָּסוּק עַד שֶׁהִקְדִּים לָזֶה הַדְּרָשׁ: "'מַרְבַדִּים עָשְׂתָה לָּהּ' (מִשְׁלֵי לא, כב) – אֵלּוּ בִּגְדֵי כְּהוּנָּה
", The Tanchuma merely interposed between the two halves of the verse by first quoting the exposition: "'She makes for herself tapestries' (Proverbs 31:22) – these are the priestly garments,"

וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (חוּלִּין נו:): "כַּרְכָא דְּכֹלָּא בֵּיהּ, מִמֶּנּוּ כֹּהֲנָיו וְכוּלֵי", וְעַל זֶה אָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ "מִפְּרִי כַפֶּיהָ נָטְעָה כָּרֶם" עַל כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

. which is based on the Gemara's statement (Chullin 56b) that Israel is like "a self-sufficient metropolis that contains everything within it—from within itself come its priests, its prophets, and its kings," and right after mentioning the priesthood it returns to "from the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard," referring to the entirety of Knesset Yisrael.

וְכֵן נִרְמַז בְּאַבְרָהָם וְשָׂרָה קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ, כְּמוֹ בְּיִצְחָק וְרִבְקָה אַחַר כָּךְ (עַיֵּין סִתְרֵי תוֹרָה לֶךְ לְךָ עט עַמּוּד ב, וּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ קכט עַמּוּד א

). And thus Abraham and Sarah symbolized the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, just as Isaac and Rebecca did afterward (see Sitrei Torah, Lech Lecha 79b, and Midrash HaNe'elam on this parashah, 129a).
וְזֶה שֶׁדָּרַשׁ "זָמְמָה שָׂדֶה" עַל שְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה – הֵ"א עִלָּאָה וְהֵ"א תַּתָּאָה
; This then is why it expounded "She considers a field" regarding the field of Machpelah—the upper Hei and the lower Hei;
וְגַן דִּלְתַתָּא נִקְרָא שָׂדֶה שֶׁל תַּפּוּחִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ "שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה'" בַּגְּמָרָא (תַּעֲנִית כט:) וּבַזֹּהַר: "חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין

", and the lower Garden (Malchut) is called an orchard of apples, as "a field which Hashem has blessed" is expounded in the Gemara (Ta'anit 29b) and in the Zohar as "the Field of Holy Apples" (Chakal Tapuchin Kadishin),

שֶׁשָּׁם מִשְׁכַּן נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ תַּפּוּחִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְרֵיחַ אַפֵּךְ כַּתַּפּוּחִים" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ז, ט), דִּמְתַרְגֵּם: "כְּרֵיחָא דְּתַפּוּחִין דְּגִנְּתָא דְּעֵדֶן

". wherein dwell the souls of Israel who are compared to apples, as it is stated: "And the fragrance of your countenance is like apples" (Song of Songs 7:9), which the Targum renders: "like the fragrance of the apples of the Garden of Eden."
וּבִכְנִיסַת שַׁבָּת שֶׁהַיִּשְׂרָאֵל מְקַבֵּל שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת, נִקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל "אֵשֶׁת חַיִל", וְהַסְּעוּדָה דְּלֵיל שַׁבָּת נִקְרֵאת סְעוּדָתָא דַּחֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין

. And therefore upon the entry of Shabbat, when a Jew accepts the observance of Shabbat, Israel is called "Eshet Chayil" (who acquires the sacred field), and the Friday night meal is called the Meal of the Field of Holy Apples.

וְדָרַשׁ בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא שָׁם: "'לֹא תִירָא לְבֵיתָהּ מִשָּׁלֶג כִּי כָל בֵּיתָהּ לָבוּשׁ שָׁנִים' (מִשְׁלֵי לא, כא) – לָמָּה לֹא תִירָא מִשָּׁלֶג (שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם)? כִּי כָל בֵּיתָהּ לָבוּשׁ שָׁנִים: אַל תִּקְרֵי שָׁנִים אֶלָּא שְׁנַיִם – שַׁבָּת וּמִילָה

". The Midrash Tanchuma there expounds further: "'She is not afraid of the snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in scarlet (shanim)' (Proverbs 31:21) – why is she not afraid of the snow (of Gehenna)? Because all her household are clothed in shanim: do not read shanim (scarlet), but shenayim (two) – Shabbat and Circumcision."
וְאַף שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם מַזְכִּיר אֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם, וְכָאן קוֹרְאוֹ "שֶׁלֶג" (גֵּיהִנָּם שֶׁל שֶׁלֶג
)? Now we must understand: why is it that everywhere else Gehenna is described as fire, whereas here the verse speaks of fearing the "snow" of Gehenna?
אַךְ עִיקַּר הַגֵּיהִנָּם הוּא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע עַצְמוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ו וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת) שֶׁהָרְשָׁעִים עוֹשִׂים גֵּיהִנָּם לְעַצְמָם מִיִּצְרָם
: The explanation is that the essence of Gehenna is generated by the evil inclination itself, as stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 6 and elsewhere):

וְיֵשׁ יֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה הַמְּכוּנֶּה בְּשֵׁם "אֵשׁ", וְכֵן יֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁל קִנְאָה וְכָבוֹד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְנוּ (וַיֵּרָא מַאֲמָר א דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וְגַם) שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ גַּם כֵּן אֵשׁ (תתק"ג מִינֵי מִיתָה = ג' פְּעָמִים אֵ"שׁ

); now the evil inclination of lust (ta'avah) is termed "fire," as are the inclinations of envy (kin'ah) and honor (kavod), as we explained above (in Vayera, Discourse 1, that the 903 varieties of death equal three times
אֵשׁ [301]); וְיֵשׁ קְלִיפַּת עֲמָלֵק, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ בַּדֶּרֶךְ" (דְּבָרִים כה, יח) – שֶׁהִצְנִינְךָ וְהִפְשִׁירְךָ מֵרְתִיחָתְךָ (רַשִּׁ"י שָׁם

), however, there is also the husk (kelipah) of Amalek, concerning whom it is stated: "how he happened upon you / cooled you (karkha) on the way" (Deuteronomy 25:18)—meaning he cooled you off and made you lukewarm from your spiritual fervor (Tanchuma Ki Teitzei 9),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּשְׁלִיךְ קְרִירוּת וְעַצְלוּת עַל הָאָדָם בעבודת ה
'. which is the inclination that casts coldness, apathy, and sluggishness (atzlut) upon a person in the service of Hashem.
וְזֶה רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה ("רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק"), וְהוּא מִתְגָּרֶה אַף בַּגְּדוֹלִים
, And this coldness is the very head and root of impurity ("Amalek is the first of the nations" Numbers 24:20), and it assails even the greatest sages,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּיַעְבֵּץ שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל: "לְבִלְתִּי עָצְבִּי" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ד, י), שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (תְּמוּרָה טז.): שֶׁלֹּא יְשַׂגְּבֵנִי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּשְׁנוֹת

, just as we find regarding Jabez, who prayed "that it may not grieve me (atzbi)" (I Chronicles 4:10), which the Gemara expounds (Temurah 16a) as: "that the evil inclination should not overpower me with heaviness and sadness to prevent me from studying Torah"—
שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנָּחָשׁ וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע נִקְרָא "עֶצֶב", שֶׁהוּא הֵבִיא עֶצֶב וְעִצָּבוֹן לָעוֹלָם ("בְּעִצָּבוֹן תֹּאכְלֶנָּה

"). for the root of the primordial serpent and the evil inclination is called sorrow and lethargy (etzev), as it brought sorrow and melancholy toil into the world ("In sorrow/toil you shall eat of it").
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לֹא תִירָא לְבֵיתָהּ מִשָּׁלֶג" – לֹא מִיבַּעְיָא מֵאֵשׁ שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה קִנְאָה וְכָבוֹד (שְׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים אֵשׁ) שֶׁלֹּא תִירָא
, And this is the meaning of "She is not afraid of the snow for her household": not only does she not fear the coarse "fire" of lust, envy, and honor,
אֶלָּא אַף מִ"שֶּׁלֶג" שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה שֶׁמַּשְׁלִיךְ עַצְלוּת וּקְרִירוּת – "לֹא תִירָא לְבֵיתָהּ", הַיְינוּ הַגְּדוֹלִים וְהַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ "בֵּיתָהּ

". but she does not even fear the "snow"—the root-husk of Amalek that casts spiritual coldness and sluggishness—for "her household," which refers to the great scholars who are called the household of the Shechinah.
לָמָּה? "כִּי כָל בֵּיתָהּ לָבוּשׁ שָׁנִים" – שְׁנַיִם: שַׁבָּת וּמִילָה
, Why? "Because all her household are clothed in two (shenayim)" – Shabbat and Circumcision,
שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם מוֹרִים שֶׁקְּשׁוּרִים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּמַאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית" – רֵאשִׁית דִּקְדוּשָּׁה, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה

: for both of these covenants demonstrate that Israel is bound at the very root to the utterance of "Bereishit" (In the beginning)—the "beginning" (Reishit) of holiness, which stands directly opposite and nullifies Amalek, the "beginning" (reishit) of impurity, one opposite the other:
מִילָה – שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה יָמִים שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת וְנַעֲשֶׂה עַל יְדֵי כֵן יִשְׂרָאֵל, מוֹרֶה שֶׁנּוֹלַד בִּקְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁקָּשׁוּר בְּרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה

; 1) Circumcision—whereby an infant is circumcised on the eighth day before possessing conscious knowledge and is thereby sealed with the sanctity of Israel—demonstrates that he is born into the intrinsic holiness of Israel, which is rooted in the primordial Beginning of divine thought ("Israel arose first in thought");
וְכֵן שַׁבָּת – שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא (כֶּתֶר, רֵאשִׁית); וּשְׁנֵיהֶם נִרְמְזוּ בְּתֵיבַת "בְּרֵאשִׁית" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (בְּרֵאשִׁית: יְרֵא שַׁבָּת, בְּרִית אֵשׁ
). and 2) Shabbat—wherein shines the revelation of Atika (Keter, the supernal Reishit); and indeed both Shabbat and Circumcision are alluded to in the anagrams of the word
בְּרֵאשִׁית (ירא שבת / ברית אש
), as written in Tikkunei Zohar.
וּמִילָה מוֹרֶה עַל "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא) – כָּל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִיקְרֵי צַדִּיק (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א צג עַמּוּד ב), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵם בֶּאֱמֶת טוֹבִים בְּעֶצֶם
; Furthermore, circumcision testifies that "Your people are all righteous" (Isaiah 60:21)—for whoever is circumcised is called righteous—meaning that in their inner essence Israel is genuinely good;

וְשַׁבָּת הוּא זְמַן תְּשׁוּבָה (שַׁבָּת נוֹטָרִיקוֹן: תָּשׁוּב), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כב) וּבְפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר (פֶּרֶק יט) בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁאַף מִי שֶׁקִּלְקֵל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יָכוֹל לְתַקֵּן הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה

. while Shabbat is the appointed time of repentance (teshuvah), as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (end of Parashah 22) and Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (ch. 19) regarding Adam the First, teaching that even one who has blemished his deeds, Heaven forbid, can rectify everything through repentance on Shabbat.

וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ב, ד): "'וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת' – זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ וְכוּלֵי, בְּאֵיזֶה זְכוּת מְמַשְׁמֶשֶׁת וּבָאָה? הַמְשֵׁל עַל הַתֵּיבָה: 'עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם' – בִּזְכוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלָה לְמַיִם (שִׁפְכוּ כַמַּיִם לִבְּכֶם

)"; And in Bereishit Rabbah (2:4) it states: "'And the spirit of God hovered' (Genesis 1:2) – this is the spirit of the Messiah; in what merit does it draw near and come? Look at the continuation of the verse: 'over the face of the waters' – in the merit of repentance, which is compared to water ('Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord' Lamentations 2:19)";
וּבַתִּיקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן לו) נִדְרַשׁ: "'עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם' – וְלֵית מַיִם אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא וְכוּלֵי
". while in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 36) it is expounded: "'over the face of the waters' – and there is no water other than Torah, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ בִּזְכוּת תּוֹרָה – שֶׁמּוֹרָה שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל טוֹבִים, שֶׁעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָא "תּוֹרָה" שֶׁמּוֹרָה לֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל לַעֲשׂוֹת רַק רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ (כְּמוֹ הַמִּילָה

); Both expositions are one and parallel Circumcision and Shabbat: 1) in the merit of the Torah—which demonstrates that Israel is intrinsically good, for it is called "Torah" because it instructs (morah) and guides the heart of Israel to do only the will of Hashem, blessed be He (paralleling circumcision);
וּבִזְכוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה – שֶׁאִם קִלְקְלוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה (כְּמוֹ הַשַּׁבָּת); וְנִרְמְזוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּמַאֲמַר בְּרֵאשִׁית

. and 2) in the merit of repentance—so that if they have stumbled, Heaven forbid, they rectify it through repentance (paralleling Shabbat); and both are thus alluded to in the opening account of Creation.

וּבַגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת פט:): "'אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ' (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יח) – אַל תִּקְרֵי כַּשָּׁנִים אֶלָּא כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית

", And in the Gemara (Shabbat 89b) it states on the verse "Though your sins be as scarlet (ka-shanim), they shall be as white as snow" (Isaiah 1:18): "Do not read ka-shanim (as scarlet), but ka-shanim (like the years)—like these years that are arranged in order from the six days of Creation";
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכָּךְ עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה לִהְיוֹת נְהוֹרָא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא, וְ"כַשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ" בְּרָזָא דִּבְרִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב צב עַמּוּד א

), meaning that it arose in the primordial Thought of Creation that the greatest light should emerge specifically out of darkness through repentance ("sins transformed into merits"), and "they shall be as white as snow" through the mystery of the Covenant of Circumcision, as written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 92a),
וְכֵן שַׁבָּת שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה כֻּלָּהּ תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (רֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה
); and likewise through Shabbat, which a person should dedicate entirely to Torah, as written at the beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah;

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל בֶּאֱמֶת טוֹבִים (עַל יְדֵי מִילָה וְתוֹרָה), וְאִם קִלְקֵל מָה, בְּשַׁבָּת הַזְּמַן לְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה כָּאָמוּר (וּלְכָךְ: "לֹא תִירָא לְבֵיתָהּ מִשָּׁלֶג כִּי כָל בֵּיתָהּ לָבוּשׁ שָׁנִים" – שַׁבָּת וּמִילָה

). signifying that in truth Israel is intrinsically good (through circumcision and Torah), and if one has blemished anything, Shabbat provides the time to rectify it through repentance and turn it white as snow—and therefore "she is not afraid of the snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in two (shanim): Shabbat and Circumcision."
וְדָרַשׁ בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא שָׁם: "'עֹז וְהָדָר לְבוּשָׁהּ וַתִּשְׂחַק לְיוֹם אַחֲרוֹן' (מִשְׁלֵי לא, כה) – אֵלּוּ עַנְנֵי כָבוֹד שֶׁהָיוּ מַקִּיפִין אֶת הָאֹהֶל שֶׁלָּהּ

". The Midrash Tanchuma there expounds further: "'Strength (oz) and splendor (hadar) are her clothing, and she laughs at the final day' (Proverbs 31:25) – these are the Clouds of Glory that surrounded Sarah's tent."
וּלְמַעְלָה בַּתַּנְחוּמָא (סִימָן ג) דָּרַשׁ: "'הוֹד וְהָדָר לָבָשְׁתָּ' (תְּהִלִּים קד, א) – מֵהוֹדְךָ וַהֲדָרְךָ הִלְבַּשְׁתָּ לְרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן

", And just before this in the Tanchuma (section 3), it expounded on the verse "'You are clothed with majesty (hod) and splendor (hadar)' (Psalms 104:1) – from Your own majesty and splendor You clothed the head of Abraham with the crown of white hair in old age, as it is stated: 'And Abraham was old' (Genesis 24:1),"
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה נח): "תָּפַשְׂתָּ אוּמָּנוּתִי, בּוֹא וּלְבוֹשׁ לְבוּשִׁי – 'וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן
'", and in Midrash Rabbah (end of Parashah 58) God says to Abraham: "You havegrasped My profession (of bestowing lovingkindness); come and wear My garment – 'And Abraham was old,'"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הַ"מַּתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה" שָׁם דְּקָאֵי עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁנִּקְרָא "עַתִּיק יוֹמִין", וּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: "לְבוּשֵׁהּ כִּתְלַג חִוָּר" (דָּנִיֵּאל ז, ט

). which the Matnot Kehunah there explains refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, being called "the Ancient of Days (Atik Yomin)," of Whom it is written: "His garment was white as snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool" (Daniel 7:9).
וּבְמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא שָׁם פָּתַח: "'ה' אֱלֹהַי גָּדַלְתָּ מְּאֹד הוֹד וְהָדָר לָבָשְׁתָּ' – הַטּוֹבָה הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁעָשִׂיתָ עִם הָאָדָם שֶׁנָּתַתָּ לוֹ זִקְנָה וְכוּלֵי

". And in Midrash Tanchuma there it opened with the beginning of that verse: "'O Hashem my God, You are very great (gadalta me'od), You are clothed with majesty and splendor' – how great is the kindness You performed with man in granting him the crown of old age, etc."
וְהָעִנְיָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ, דְּשֵׁם "גָּדוֹל" מוֹרֶה בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר, וְ"גָּדַלְתָּ מְּאֹד" הַיְינוּ בְּלֹא סוֹף וְתַכְלִית – אֵין סוֹף

. The inner meaning of this verse is as we have explained: the term "great" (gadol) signifies that which is beyond measure, and "You are very great (gadalta me'od)" refers to the Infinite (Ein Sof) without end or limit.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶאֱצִיל עֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת לִבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם
, And from His infinite essence, Hashem, blessed be He, emanated ten attributes (the ten sefirot) for the creation of the world,

וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּחְשַׁב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (דְּבָרִים רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת וָאֶתְחַנַּן וּבְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד, י, וּבִפְסִיקְתָּא דְּרַב כַּהֲנָא שׂוֹשׂ אָשִׂישׂ לְגִירְסַת הַיַּלְקוּט, עַיֵּין שָׁם הֵיטֵב) עֲשָׂרָה לְבוּשִׁים שֶׁלָּבַשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִיּוֹם שֶׁבָּרָא הָעוֹלָם, וְהַיְינוּ עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת שֶׁהֵם עֲשָׂרָה לְבוּשִׁים

. which corresponds to what is enumerated in the Midrash (Devarim Rabbah at the end of Va'etchanan; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:10; and Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, Sos Asis, according to the text of the Yalkut Shimoni, see there well): the ten garments that the Holy One, blessed be He, donned from the day He created the world—namely the ten sefirot, which are ten garments.
וְחָשַׁב בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא הַלְּבוּשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן: "הוֹד וְהָדָר לָבָשְׁתָּ" (תְּהִלִּים קד, א), וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁקְּשׁוּרִים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ

; And the Pesikta counts as the very first garment: "You are clothed with majesty (hod) and splendor (hadar)" (Psalms 104:1), which corresponds to Keter Elyon (the Supernal Crown, Atik Yomin), bound to the Infinite Root;
שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ כְּתִיב הַלְּבוּשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי: "עֹטֶה אוֹר כַּשַּׂלְמָה" (שָׁם קד, ב) – מַאֲמַר "יְהִי אוֹר" שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד חָכְמָה

. for immediately following it in the next verse is written the second garment: "Who covers Himself with light as with a cloak" (Psalms 104:2)—which is the utterance "Let there be light," corresponding to Chokhmah (Wisdom).

וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁדָּרַשׁ הַתַּנְחוּמָא (חַיֵּי שָׂרָה ג): "'הוֹד' – זֶה הָעֹז שֶׁהִלְבַּשְׁתִּיךָ בַּיָּם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ (שְׁמוֹת טו, ב); 'וְהָדָר' – הַהָדָר שֶׁנֶּהְדַּרְתָּ בִּי בְּסִינַי וְכוּלֵי

". And this illuminates what the Tanchuma expounds there (Chayei Sarah 3): "'Majesty (hod)' – this is the strength (oz) with which you clothed Me at the Sea, as it is stated: 'My strength (ozi) and song is Yah' (Exodus 15:2); 'and splendor (hadar)' – this is the splendor with which you glorified Me at Sinai, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבַּיָּם וּבְסִינַי הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא (כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן, לְבוּשׁ "הוֹד וְהָדָר
"): The explanation is that both at the Splitting of the Sea and at Mount Sinai there occurred a direct revelation of Atika (Keter Elyon, the first garment of "hod ve-hadar"):

דִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף בְּעַתִּיקָא תַּלְיָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב נב עַמּוּד ב), וְאִיתָא בַּמְּכִילְתָּא (וּבַזֹּהַר שָׁם סד עַמּוּד ב): "רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה יְחֶזְקֵאל

"; for the splitting of the Red Sea depended upon Atika, as is written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 52b), and as stated in the Mekhilta (and Zohar there, 64b): "A maidservant saw at the Sea what the prophet Ezekiel did not see";

וְכֵן בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה כְּתִיב: "פָּנִים בְּפָנִים דִּבֶּר ה' עִמָּכֶם" (דְּבָרִים ה, ד), וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פב עַמּוּד א): "חָמוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָכָא מַה דְּלָא חָמָא יְחֶזְקֵאל", וְהַיְינוּ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא

, and similarly at the Giving of the Torah it is written: "Face to face Hashem spoke with you" (Deuteronomy 5:4), on which the holy Zohar states (Part II, 82a): "Israel beheld here at Sinai what Ezekiel did not behold"—namely the revelation of Atika—
וְכֵן אִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנו עַמּוּד ב) דְּ"אָנֹכִי" בֵּיהּ כ' כֶּתֶר, עַיֵּין שָׁם; וְזֶהוּ לְבוּשׁ "הוֹד וְהָדָר
". and likewise it is stated (Zohar Part III, 256b) that the word
אָנֹכִי
("I am") contains the letter Kaf of Keter, see there; and this is the supernal garment of "majesty and splendor" (hod ve-hadar).

וּמַסִּיק בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא שָׁם: כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּסִינַי "נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע", עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ב), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁזֶּה הַהָדָר שֶׁנִּתְהַדַּרְתָּ בִּי בְּסִינַי נֶגֶד כָּל הָעַמִּים

; The Midrash Tanchuma concludes there that once Israel proclaimed at Sinai "We will do and we will hear (na'aseh ve-nishma)," concerning this it was stated: "As a rose among the thorns, so is my beloved among the daughters" (Song of Songs 2:2)—for this was the splendor (hadar) with which God was glorified by Israel at Sinai in contrast to all the nations who refused the Torah;

וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ "נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע" נִכְתְּרוּ בִּשְׁנֵי כְּתָרִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פח.), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּלְּבוּשׁ "הוֹד וְהָדָר" נַעֲשֶׂה לָהֶם אוֹר מַקִּיף – שְׁנֵי כְּתָרִים עַל הָרֹאשׁ

. and at the moment Israel said "We will do and we will hear," each Jew was crowned with two crowns (Shabbat 88a)—meaning that from the supernal garment of "majesty and splendor" (hod ve-hadar) there was formed for them a Surrounding Light (Ohr Makif) of two crowns upon their heads.

וּמַה שֶּׁדָּרַשׁ "הוֹד" עַל הָעֹז שֶׁהִלְבַּשְׁתִּיךָ עַל הַיָּם, הוּא דְּבַיָּם אִיתָא בַּמְּכִילְתָּא עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חֹמָה" (שְׁמוֹת יד, כט) חָסֵר ו': "אַל תִּקְרֵי חוֹמָה אֶלָּא חֵמָה", עַיֵּין שָׁם

, Now the reason the Midrash expounded "majesty (hod)" as the "strength (oz)" at the Red Sea, and "splendor (hadar)" as the revelation at Sinai, is that at the Sea it is stated in the Mekhilta on the second verse "and the waters were a wall (
חֹמָה
, spelled defective without a Vav) unto them" (Exodus 14:29): "Do not read chomah (a wall), but chemah (wrath)," see there—

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה קִטְרוּג עַל הַיָּם ("הַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה"), רַק יִשְׂרָאֵל עָשׂוּ תְּשׁוּבָה, וְזֶהוּ "עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם" – תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלָה לְמַיִם

; meaning that the prosecuting angel leveled an accusation against Israel at the Sea, and they were saved because Israel repented in heartfelt prayer and self-sacrifice into the sea, corresponding to "over the face of the waters"—repentance, which is compared to water;
וְ"הָדָר" דָּרַשׁ עַל מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, דִּכְתִיב בּוֹ: "אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם" (תְּהִלִּים פב, ו), שֶׁפָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָתָן וְנַעֲשׂוּ בֶּאֱמֶת טוֹבִים, וְזֶהוּ תּוֹרָה

; whereas "splendor (hadar)" is expounded regarding the Giving of the Torah at Sinai, concerning which it is written: "I said: You are divine beings" (Psalms 82:6), when their impurity ceased and they were revealed as intrinsically good, which is the aspect of Torah;
וּמִשְּׁנֵיהֶם נַעֲשֶׂה אַחַר כָּךְ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה אוֹר מַקִּיף וּשְׁנֵי כְּתָרִים
. and out of both of these (repentance at the Sea and Torah at Sinai) were formed the Surrounding Light and the two crowns at the Giving of the Torah.

וְזֶה שֶׁדָּרַשׁ בְּשָׂרָה: "'עֹז וְהָדָר לְבוּשָׁהּ' – אֵלּוּ עַנְנֵי כָבוֹד": "עֹז" – לְבוּשׁ הוֹד מֵהַיָּם עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה ("עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ"), וְ"הָדָר" – שֶׁל סִינַי שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל טוֹבִים בֶּאֱמֶת

, And this is why the Midrash expounds regarding Sarah: "'Strength (oz) and splendor (hadar) are her clothing' – these are the Clouds of Glory": for "strength (oz)" is the garment of hod from the Sea through repentance, and "splendor (hadar)" is the garment of Sinai testifying that Israel is intrinsically good,
וּמִשְּׁנֵיהֶם זָכוּ לְאוֹר מַקִּיף, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: "אֵלּוּ עַנְנֵי כָבוֹד שֶׁהָיוּ מַקִּיפִין אֶת הָאֹהֶל שֶׁלָּהּ
". and from the union of both she merited the Surrounding Light (Ohr Makif) of Keter—which is why the Midrash explains: "these are the Clouds of Glory that surrounded her tent."
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּסוֹף הַפָּסוּק: "וַתִּשְׂחַק לְיוֹם אַחֲרוֹן" – דִּכְתִיב: "אָז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ" (תְּהִלִּים קכו, ב), וְהַיְינוּ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא

, And this explains why that verse concludes: "and she laughs (va-tischak) at the final day"—for it is written: "Then (az) our mouth shall be filled with laughter (sechok)" (Psalms 126:2), which occurs at the revelation of Atika,

שֶׁכֵּן מוֹרֶה לְשׁוֹן "אָז", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב נד עַמּוּד א) עַל "אָז יָשִׁיר": "כַּד אִתְנְהִיר נְהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא וְכוּלֵי, וְאָלֶ"ף אִנְקִיב בַּחֲשׁוֹכֵי וְנָהִיר לְכָל עֵיבָר וְכוּלֵי וּמָטוּ לְזַיִ"ן", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. as the word
אָז
("then") signifies, in accordance with what is written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 54a) on "Then (
אז
) sang Moses": "when the illumination of Atika shines forth, the Alef (1, Keter) pierces the darkness and illuminates in every direction until reaching Zayin (7, Malchut)," see there.

וְעִיקָּרוֹ הוּא לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא ("לְיוֹם אַחֲרוֹן"), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קכז עַמּוּד א), וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁזָּכוּ לְהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "עֹז וְהָדָר לְבוּשָׁהּ", כְּתִיב: "וַתִּשְׂחַק לְיוֹם אַחֲרוֹן

". Now the full manifestation of "Then our mouth shall be filled with laughter" belongs to the World to Come ("the final day"), as written in Midrash HaNe'elam on this parashah (127a) and in the Gemara (Berakhot 31a: "It is forbidden for a person to fill his mouth with laughter in this world, until it is stated 'Then our mouth shall be filled with laughter'"); nevertheless, to the extent that the righteous already merit a foretaste of the revelation of Atika ("Strength and splendor are her clothing"), it is written: "and she laughs toward the final day."
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא בְּרַב בְּרוּנָא (בְּרָכוֹת ט:): "זִמְנָא חֲדָא סְמַךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה וְלָא פְּסַק חוּכָא מִפּוּמֵיהּ כּוּלָּא יוֹמָא" – וְהַיְינוּ מִמְּלֹא שְׂחוֹק פִּיו

! Indeed, we find in the Gemara (Berakhot 9b) regarding Rav Beruna: "Once he joined redemption (ge'ulah) to prayer (tefillah) in the morning service, and laughter did not cease from his mouth the entire day"—which was an actual manifestation of filling his mouth with holy laughter!
אַךְ סְמִיכוּת גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה מוֹרֶה עַל הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא
: And the reason why joining redemption to prayer brought this about is that joining redemption to prayer taps into the revelation of Atika:
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סוֹף פֶּרֶק א דִּבְרָכוֹת): "הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע צָרִיךְ לְהַזְכִּיר בָּהּ קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף וּמַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת וְכוּלֵי

"; for as they taught in the Yerushalmi (end of the first chapter of Berakhot): "One who recites the Shema (in the blessing of Ge'ulah right before the Amidah) must mention within it the Splitting of the Red Sea and the Plague of the Firstborn";

וּמַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת הִיא מַכָּה עֲשִׂירִית, שֶׁבָּהּ נִתְבָּרְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיָצְאוּ מִקְּלִיפָּה עֲשִׂירִית – רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה – וְנִכְנְסוּ לִקְדוּשָּׁה בְּמִדָּה עֲשִׂירִית שֶׁהוּא כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן

now the Plague of the Firstborn was the tenth plague, through which Israel was completely extracted from the tenth and highest husk—the root-husk of impurity—and entered into the tenth and highest attribute of holiness, which is Keter Elyon (Atika) (

שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה בְּכָל הַמַּכּוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נָגֹף וְרָפוֹא" [יְשַׁעְיָה יט, כב] – נָגוֹף לְמִצְרַיִם וְרָפוֹא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב לו עַמּוּד א, וְסֵדֶר הָעֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת הָיָה מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שָׁם כט סוֹף עַמּוּד א

), (for so it operated across all ten plagues, as it is stated: "smiting and healing" Isaiah 19:22—each plague smote a husk of Egypt and simultaneously healed the corresponding sefirah in Israel, as written in the holy Zohar, Part II, 36a, and the progression of the ten plagues ascended from below to above, from Malchut up to Keter, as written in the Zohar there, 29a end),
וּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף בְּעַתִּיקָא תַּלְיָא
; and the Splitting of the Red Sea likewise depended directly upon Atika;
וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁזָּכָה רַב בְּרוּנָא לִסְמִיכַת גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, הַיְינוּ שֶׁזָּכָה לְהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְלָכֵן לֹא פְּסַק חוּכָא מִפּוּמֵיהּ

. consequently, when Rav Beruna merited the complete union of Ge'ulah (which draws down the light of Atika from the Plague of the Firstborn and the Splitting of the Sea) with Tefillah (Malchut / the Shechinah), he experienced the illumination of Atika—a foretaste of the World to Come—and therefore holy joy and laughter did not cease from his mouth the entire day.
וְכֵן כָּאן: "עֹז וְהָדָר לְבוּשָׁהּ וַתִּשְׂחַק לְיוֹם אַחֲרוֹן
". And so it is right here regarding Sarah (and Knesset Yisrael on Shabbat): "Strength and splendor are her clothing, and she laughs at the final day."

sections.title: Chayei Sarah — Teaching 2
sections.summary: The Spiritual Meaning of Sarah’s Years

pairs: שְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה נִקְרָא "שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה'" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (קכח עַמּוּד ב
). The field of Machpelah is called "a field which Hashem has blessed" (Genesis 27:27), as is written in the holy Zohar (Chayei Sarah 128b).

וְאַחַר הָעֲקֵידָה, כְּשֶׁנִּשְׁלַם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּכָל הָעֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים" – בְּאִינּוּן יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (קכט עַמּוּד א) – אָז קָנָה שְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה לִקְבוּרַת שָׂרָה

. And following the Binding of Isaac, once Abraham our father, peace be upon him, had reached completion in all ten sefirotic attributes—as it is stated: "And Abraham was old, well-advanced in days," meaning he entered into those supernal days (the ten sefirot), as written in the holy Zohar (129a)—he then purchased the field of Machpelah for the burial of Sarah.
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (קכז עַמּוּד א) שֶׁנִּפְתַּח לוֹ פֶּתַח גַּן עֵדֶן שָׁם, וְאָמַר (שָׁם עַמּוּד ב) דַּהֲוָה סָלֵיק רֵיחִין עִלָּאִין וְחָמָא נְהוֹרָא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ מְעַרְתָּא וְכוּלֵי

; It is related in the holy Zohar (127a) that the gateway to Gan Eden opened before him there, and it states (127b) that supernal fragrances wafted upward and he beheld a radiant light shining forth from within the cave, etc.;
וְזֶה רֵיחַ "שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה'" – רֵיחַ גַּן עֵדֶן
; now this fragrance was the scent of "a field which Hashem has blessed"—the aroma of Gan Eden;
וּ"נְהוֹרָא" הַיְינוּ מֵאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּגְנַז בַּתּוֹרָה
, and the "radiant light" was the primordial light of Creation that was hidden away in the Torah,
וַחֲמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים אוֹרָה שֶׁבְּפָרָשַׁת "יְהִי אוֹר" הֵם כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (ג, ה
), where the five occurrences of the word "light" in the passage "Let there be light" correspond to the Five Books of the Torah (Bereishit Rabbah 3:5),
וְהַיְינוּ אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּשְׁנֵי לוּחוֹת הַבְּרִית שֶׁהֵם תְּרֵי הֵהִין (ה' דִּבְּרוֹת בְּלוּחַ זֶה וְה' דִּבְּרוֹת בְּלוּחַ זֶה

), which is also the light of the Torah engraved upon the Two Tablets of the Covenant, corresponding to the two letters Hei of the Tetragrammaton (five commandments on one tablet and five on the other),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּהַקְדָּמַת תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (יג עַמּוּד א): "חָמֵשׁ לְגוֹ חָמֵשׁ אִילֵּין ה' ה', וּמֵאִילֵּין אִתְיְהִיבוּ עֲשַׂר דִּבְרִין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
", as is written in the Introduction to Tikkunei Zohar (13a): "Five within five—these are the upper Hei and lower Hei, and from these were given the Ten Commandments of the Torah,"
וְזֶה נִרְמַז גַּם בִּשְׂדֵה הַמַּכְפֵּלָה – הֵ"א דְּבִשְׁמָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּאִיהִי מַכְפֵּלָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
. and this very mystery is alluded to in the field of ha-Machpelah—the letter Hei of the Holy Name which is doubled (five and five, making ten), as written in the holy Zohar.

וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה נח, ח): "כַּמָּה דְּיוֹאוֹת נִשְׁתַּפְּכוּ, כַּמָּה קוּלְמוֹסִין נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ לִכְתּוֹב 'בְּנֵי חֵת' עֲשָׂרָה פְּעָמִים בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ! עֲשָׂרָה פְּעָמִים כְּנֶגֶד עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת, לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁמְּבָרֵר מִקָּחוֹ שֶׁל צַדִּיק כְּאִלּוּ מְקַיֵּים עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת

". Now in Midrash Rabbah (Parashah 58:8) it states: "How much ink was spilled and how many quills were broken to write 'the children of Heth (Bnei Chet)' ten times in this chapter! Ten times corresponding to the Ten Commandments, to teach you that whoever clarifies and ratifies the purchase of a righteous man is accounted as though he fulfilled the Ten Commandments."
וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין מַה טִּיבָם שֶׁל בְּנֵי חֵת לַעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת שֶׁיּוּזְכְּרוּ עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים כְּנֶגְדָּם
? We must understand: what connection do the pagan children of Heth have to the Ten Commandments that their name should be recorded ten times in the Torah corresponding to them?
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד
:): However, the matter is understood based on what is taught in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 44b):

כְּשֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיחֶזְקֵאל לֵךְ אֱמוֹר לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: "אָבִיךְ הָאֱמֹרִי וְאִמֵּךְ חִתִּית" (יְחֶזְקֵאל טז, ג), אָמְרָה רוּחַ הַפִּסְקוֹנִית לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, אִם יָבוֹאוּ אַבְרָהָם וְשָׂרָה וְיַעַמְדוּ לְפָנֶיךָ, אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לָהֶם כָּךְ וּמַכְלִימָם

?! When the Holy One, blessed be He, told Ezekiel, "Go say to Israel: 'Your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite'" (Ezekiel 16:3), the interceding spirit said before the Holy One, blessed be He: "Master of the Universe! If Abraham and Sarah were to come and stand before You, would You say this to them and put them to shame?!"
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י שָׁם: שֶׁתֶּרַח וַאֲבוֹתָיו מֵאֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן בָּאוּ (אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁם גָּרוּ), עַיֵּין שָׁם
. And Rashi there explains that Terach and his ancestors had sojourned in the land of Canaan, see there.
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין, דְּהָא תֶּרַח מִבְּנֵי שֵׁם כִּמְפוֹרָשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה וּמֵהֶם יָצְאוּ אַבְרָהָם וְשָׂרָה, וְלָמָּה נִקְרְאוּ אֱמֹרִי וְחִתִּית

? Yet this requires deeper understanding, for Terach descended from Shem (not Canaan), as is explicit in the Torah, and from him came Abraham and Sarah—so in what sense is Abraham called "your Amorite father" and Sarah "your Hittite mother"?
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב רַבֵּינוּ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא מִלּוּבְּלִין בְּסֵפֶר "דִּבְרֵי אֱמֶת" (פָּרָשַׁת לֶךְ לְךָ
